0.original: Y'shtola's eyes seem to be staring into your very soul.

25.original: Speak with Alisaie at the Inn at Journey's Head.

48.original: At such moments, it is hard to know what to say...<hex:02100103>...Are you all right, my friend?

49.original: You did well, <hex:022C0DFF07022903EB0203FF02200203>─you and the Exarch...

50.original: Shortly after you left, we observed that our enemy's ranks were no longer being replenished─presumably when your absence was noted. So we polished them off and came as quickly as we could.

51.original: ...Which is to say, not quickly enough. But then you had the Exarch for company, didn't you, and you could ask for no better than that.

52.original: Ere we descended from the throne room, I did chance upon an object which, if I have the right of it, did once─

53.original: ...Hm. M-Mine apologies. Mayhap now is not an appropriate time. Let us speak of it later.

54.original: The only way is forward. So I have to believe that whatever lies ahead will be better than what came before.

55.original: <hex:022C0DFF07022903EB0203FF02200203>. If you are ready, would you recount to us how the day unfolded?

56.original: ...So you reached out to Elidibus at the last...and his heart was moved.

58.original: I'm not sure I did the right thing.

60.original: I only did as you asked.

61.original: Perhaps you did. Perhaps you did not. None can say.

62.original: Perhaps not. Ultimately, you had no choice but to strike him down.

64.original: But the important thing is this: though violence proved unavoidable, you did at least come to understand your foe.

65.original: And in knowing his hopes and dreams do we best remember him─him and his legacy.

66.original: So long as they remain unforgotten, the love he and his brethren bore for one another and the star may yet be rewarded.

67.original: You said that an ancient came to your aid. But how is that possible?

68.original: A gift from Emet-Selch. He knew of Elidibus's plight. Foreseeing his own death, he made provisions to bring Elidibus's suffering to an end, lest his friend be left to continue the struggle alone.

69.original: Or so I wildly speculate. It is unlikely we will ever know the truth.

70.original: The best we can do is to remember events as they happened, no more and no less. As the Ronkans so rightly put it, “History is learned, not lived.”

72.original: My friend! We were given to understand thou wert injured. Shouldst thou not be abed?

73.original: Lie down at a time like this!? Don't be absurd! I would have come sooner had the guards not made such a fuss!

74.original: Now, tell me what's happened. Where is the Exarch?

76.original: <hex:022C0DFF07022903EB0203FF02200203>... Will you show me his spirit vessel?

77.original: Yes... Both his soul and memories seem intact. Good.

78.original: Unlike the others, his aether was not highly charged, and so it did not seem necessary to employ a familiar for the imbuing. But I needed to be certain all the same. Oh, what a relief...

79.original: Then 'tis but a question of restoring his soul unto his flesh.

80.original: And as thou didst lately tell me, the success of this process resteth on no more than our friend's soul recognizing his flesh as its own.

81.original: Given his apparent desire to return to the Source with <hex:022C0DFF07022903EB0203FF02200203>, one would think his soul would be only too happy to be home, no? Surely it wouldn't balk at the relative newness of its accommodation?

82.original: So one would hope, but none can speak for the Exarch's heart of hearts. And he can no longer speak for himself.

83.original: Furthermore, though I have drawn upon all of my not inconsiderable experience to predict the outcome, the fact remains that there is no direct precedent for what we are attempting.

84.original: Will his body accept his soul? Will his essences blend properly? Will he awaken whole of mind? Any number of things could go awry.

85.original: ...Assuming I have succeeded in tempering your expectations, I should probably add that I <hex:021A020203>did<hex:021A020103> ask the Exarch if he still wished to return to the Source in full knowledge of the risks.

86.original: A simple enough question, one would think, warranting a single-word reply. Yet the answer I received was rather longer than that. Almost comically so, in fact. Regardless, out of respect for the man, I shall attempt to recite it─with a certain amount of poetic license. Ahem!

87.original: “As I grew older, the burdens I carried became ever more numerous. Burdens which weighed upon my hopes, burying them deep within my breast. So deep that I couldn't be certain they were still there.

88.original: “But when I look around me, I am reminded that, no matter how deeply buried they may be, our hopes never truly disappear. No, they are always with us. Guiding us. Driving us.

89.original: “I see it in Vauthry, who sought to vindicate his existence by creating his paradise.

90.original: “I see it in Ran'jit, who forsook his life's cause in order to protect that which he held most dear.

91.original: “I see it in the people, who chose to struggle rather than surrender to despair.

92.original: “And though our struggles may differ greatly, since the very beginning of time, they have all shared that one common thread: hope.

93.original: “We struggle because we have hope. And when the time comes, I too will embrace mine. I will follow my heart, regardless of the risks.

94.original: “And I will live with all my being, as befits one who has been granted a second chance.”

95.original: There! I told you it was long. And unspeakably sentimental to boot. One would think them the outpourings of a dewy-eyed boy, not the <hex:021A020203>old man<hex:021A020103> the Exarch seems to believe he is.

96.original: I mean, <hex:021A020203>really<hex:021A020103>─he's scarcely been alive as long as I've been in hiding!

97.original: I daresay he is blushing in his vessel.

98.original: Speaking of which, we should make ready for our journey. Time remains of the essence, after all.

99.original: Needless to say, once we leave, there is no guarantee that we can return. If anyone has unfinished business, now is the time to see to it.

100.original: I must pay a visit to Slitherbough. Let us reconvene here anon.

101.original: Hm... There remain some few matters which require mine attention in Il Mheg.

102.original: May I leave Thancred in thy care, child?

103.original: Um...I've been meaning to get some flowers. For Minfilia.

104.original: I thought you might help me choose them. And then we could go to Nabaath Areng together...one last time.

106.original: Well, it's back to Eulmore for me. Amongst other things, I owe the mayor an apology about his airship.

107.original: I assume you have places of your own to be, Alisaie. I shall see you later.

108.original: I shall take this opportunity to conduct a final inspection of the spirit vessels. Given what is at stake, one can never be too thorough.

109.original: As you've probably guessed, I'm going to pay a visit to the Inn at Journey's Head. But I want you to come too.

110.original: I realize you don't need to say any farewells.

111.original: But the Exarch does, if only in spirit. So I thought you might bring him along, so to speak.

112.original: I'm sure he'd love the thought of being lugged about on his hero's back.

113.original: So let's be off, shall we? I can't wait to see how Halric's doing!

114.original: Halric? Halric! Oh gods, don't tell me he's wandered off again?

115.original: Quickly, <hex:022C0DFF07022903EB0203FF02200203>! We have to find him!

116.original: Oh, Alisaie! I didn't see you there. If you're looking for Halric, he's gone for a walk with one of the others. They were planning to visit the graveyard, if I'm not mistaken.

117.original: Well, that's a relief. Shall we adjourn to the graveyard, then?

119.original: Oh, greetings, <hex:022C0DFF07022903EB0203FF02200203>! Looking for Halric, by any chance?

120.original: There he is. I was afraid he'd wandered off again.

121.original: Oh, there's no need to worry─Halric's safe and well. He's been showing good progress, and likes to go for walks of late.

122.original: Though his steps usually bring him to this particular spot...

123.original: Oh? I wasn't aware he had family here.

124.original: He doesn't. It's Tesleen. Her sword, that is.

125.original: We buried it here in her honor.

127.original: What brings you back so soon, out of interest? I didn't think the next round of treatments was due yet.

128.original: Uh...no. It isn't. Look─I realize this is sudden...but I've come to say good-bye. It's time for me to return home.

129.original: But rest assured the treatments will continue. Beq Lugg will come to oversee them in my stead.

130.original: I see... You did mention that you and your friends were searching for a way home.

131.original: Needless to say, we'll be sorry to see you go─but I know everyone will be happy for you. Truly.

132.original: Happy and grateful. You've done so much for us. Achieved what none of us dared hope was possible.

133.original: And we'll see to it that your good work continues, and that no more poor souls are buried here before their time.

134.original: So rest easy, and take care. We wish you every happiness.

135.original: Thank you. I will miss you all.

136.original: But it isn't time to say our farewells quite yet. So if there are any tasks that need doing─hunting beasts, fetching water, and what have you─just say the word.

137.original: I mean to make use of every last moment here. After all...

138.original: The time left to you...is precious...

139.original: That's right, Halric... That's exactly right.

140.original: Those words will guide you true. So never forget them.

143.original: Thank you for coming to see Halric, <hex:022C0DFF07022903EB0203FF02200203>. And Tesleen as well.

144.original: She did always enjoy having visitors. And none were more welcome than you and Alisaie.

145.original: <hex:021A020203>What<hex:021A020103>? I'm not crying! I just have sand in my eye, that's all.

146.original: ...Ahem. As I mentioned, I mean to stay here as long as possible. In the meantime, perhaps you could go and look in on the others?

147.original: Alphinaud, for instance. If <hex:021A020203>anyone<hex:021A020103> is crying, it will be him!

148.original: What are you still doing here? Hurry over to Eulmore and look in on Alphinaud. Oh, and send my regards to the Chais.

149.original: I hear the airship crashed in Amh Araeng. Never mind. The important thing is you're all safe and well.

150.original: That said, we should probably retrieve the wreck before the locals strip it for trolley parts. Or perhaps we can make a trade of it...

151.original: Oh, thank goodness <hex:021A020203>you<hex:021A020103> can still return! If I had to bid farewell to you both, my heart would burst here and now!

152.original: Like Alphinaud, I know that yours is a life of constant employment, but do visit us from time to time. It would mean the world to us.

153.original: I understand the Exarch will be leaving with you. Capable though its custodians are, the Crystarium will be poorer for his absence.

154.original: It seems the coming years will be a period of transition for both of our cities... But through mutual cooperation, I am confident we will find a way forward.

155.original: 'Tis a strange feeling, <hex:022C0DFF07022903EB0203FF02200203>. To stand in the company of our friends, knowing that I will never see them again... I struggle to reconcile it in my mind.

156.original: But this I know: I shall cherish my memories of Norvrandt─of every soul I met here─for the rest of my days.

157.original: And I shall look forward to your tales of their endeavors.
